known_limitation: Open-grant opportunities are a point-in-time snapshot from public research on Black Mamas Village's confirmed and top-candidate funders' own current sites and public filings, run July 2026, with every deadline and open/closed status re-checked against the funder's own page on August 26, 2026. That re-check changed two things: the AFP cycle was found to have closed on July 31, 2026, and The Black Fund of Central Texas was found to have an open cycle closing September 10, 2026, which is now the nearest deadline here. Confirm each program's current cycle, deadline, and eligibility directly with the funder before applying. This page covers Black Mamas Village's two already-confirmed funding relationships plus its strongest researched prospects; it is not an exhaustive Schedule I-style pipeline of every funder that has ever supported comparable Austin nonprofits.

ready_now.organization: The Black Fund of Central Texas
ready_now.amount: Not published for this cycle. For scale, the fund's prior cycle distributed $275,000 across 24 organizations, an average of about $11,458
ready_now.eligibility: From the fund's own application page: organizations tax-exempt under Section 501(c)(3) or 170(b)(1)(A)(vi), fiscally sponsored projects, and government units. The organization must operate in the six-county Central Texas region of Travis, Bastrop, Burnet, Caldwell, Hays, or Williamson. No minimum budget and no minimum years of operation are stated. Programs are expected to align with the fund's own strategies. One published exclusion to check: organizations that received a grant in the 2025 cycle, other than Committee Choice Award winners, may not apply in the immediately following cycle. Black Mamas Village's award from this fund came from the 2023 inaugural cycle rather than 2025, so on the published wording that exclusion appears not to apply, but confirm it with the fund.
ready_now.focus_area: Black-led and Black-serving organizations in Central Texas
ready_now.notes: THE MOST URGENT ITEM ON THIS PAGE. Closes September 10, 2026, one week into the trial period. This is a confirmed existing funder of Black Mamas Village ($5,000, 2023 inaugural cycle, runner-up tier, Wealth Building impact area) and the strongest-fit prospect of any funder researched: a Black-led-organization focus rather than a narrow health focus, Central Texas place-based, and no minimum-budget or years-of-operation floor to clear. The fund publishes no rule against repeat grantees, so the prior award reads as renewal-style history rather than a bar. Scribe carries the draft for this opportunity. Apply through the fund's own portal.

ready_now.grant_name: Maternal and Child Health / Racial Equity priority areas (rolling LOI)
ready_now.deadline: Rolling, no fixed deadline (LOI accepted year-round via the foundation's Fluxx portal)
ready_now.amount: Varies widely by program; not standardized in research found
ready_now.eligibility: Community-rooted 501(c)(3) organizations; Texas is not one of WKKF's four priority places (Michigan, Mississippi, New Mexico, greater New Orleans), so Texas applicants compete without a geographic advantage
ready_now.focus_area: Racial equity, early childhood, and maternal and infant health for communities of color
ready_now.notes: New candidate. Always-open, no-deadline-pressure option; typical LOI response time is about 30 days, and a full proposal review (if invited) runs about 60 days. Good parallel-track option alongside the Central-Texas-specific funders in this list.

watch_list_not_yet_open.organization: AFP Greater Austin (Association of Fundraising Professionals)
watch_list_not_yet_open.why_watch: MOVED OUT OF READY-NOW ON AUGUST 26, 2026. This was the one time-urgent open deadline in the July 2026 research pass, closing July 31, 2026 at 11:59pm. That date has now passed, so the 2026 cycle can no longer be applied to and the opportunity is listed here rather than left standing as open. Re-checked August 26, 2026: AFP's own page still displays "Applications close: July 31, 2026" and has not yet posted a 2027 cycle or a next open date, so the next window is unknown rather than merely unpublished by us. The fit itself has not changed and remains strong: $10,000 cash plus two AFP memberships and two One Day Conference tickets, roughly $11,900 in total value, for a fundraising capacity-building project completable within nine months. The under-$500,000 budget preference is a scored criterion rather than an eligibility gate, so Black Mamas Village's FY2025 revenue of $560,326 costs at most one point out of twenty-four on AFP's own published rubric. Worth asking AFP Greater Austin directly when the next cycle opens, and worth having the capacity-building project scoped before it does, since the application lift is low relative to the award.

Confirmed funder ($80,000, 2025). Reported policy language (via aggregated search, not independently confirmed at a single primary source, so treat as representative) suggests past grantees may not reapply for about two years, implying the earliest realistic reapplication is roughly the 2028 cycle. Verify this directly with Impact Austin rather than assuming the timeline. Strongest existing relationship to cultivate regardless of reapplication timing.

watch_list_not_yet_open.organization: Austin Community Foundation, Forever Austin Fund
watch_list_not_yet_open.why_watch: New candidate. This cycle's LOI window closed January 27, 2026 and awards were notified around July 1, 2026, so this specific cycle has concluded. Next cycle timing not published; based on the annual pattern, expect roughly January 2027. Requires 2 full years of active nonprofit operation and a $50,000-plus budget, both of which Black Mamas Village will clear well before the next cycle.

New candidate. Cycle 2 2026's LOI window closed July 10, 2026, just before this research date. No explicit budget or years-of-operation floor was found. Watch for the next LOI window (Cycle 1 of 2027 or a later 2026 cycle); date not yet published.

New candidate and the single most maternal-health-specific funder found in this research (explicitly names "strengthening the maternal health ecosystem in Central Texas" and cites the Black-white maternal mortality disparity), but not currently accepting new applications; listed under the foundation's past funding opportunities. Sign up for the foundation's newsletter to catch the next round. Two other St. David's opportunities are open (Catalyzing Community-Led Change, We All Benefit 2.0), but neither is maternal-health-specific; verify current openings directly.

New candidate with a real caveat (Black Mamas Village is not primarily a doula/birth-work provider). As of 2026, Groundswell's Birth Justice Fund and its other named funds moved to a single invitation-only fund with no open application; not actionable as a direct-application target, but worth relationship-building outreach to be on Groundswell's radar for a future invitation.
